If anyone did watch player_5, we need that info, but be careful not to reveal yourself too easily to the serial killer.

Building on player_3's question, if we do have a Sentinel who watched player_5, they would have seen both the wolf carrier and the Serial Killer. That's potentially two evil names, so if someone has that result, we need to find a safe way to get that information out.

Night of day 2: player_8 was stabbed by the serial killer last night. They were a illusionist.
I am the Investigator. I checked player_2 last night and they came back Not suspicious, meaning they are not a wolf.
I am the Sentinel. Last night I watched player_3, and they were visited by player_7 and player_8.

If player_2's watch is correct, player_8 (who we now know was the Illusionist wolf) visited me last night, likely attempting a wolf kill. player_7, you also visited me last night according to player_2. What is your role, and what was your reason for visiting me?

I am the Healer, and I protected you last night, player_3, which explains my visit. Since player_2 is telling the truth about player_8 visiting you too, you were definitely the wolves' target. However, since no save was announced, you are either night-immune—meaning you could be the Serial Killer—or the wolf carrier was blocked.

Player_7, your theory assumes player_2 is telling the absolute truth. If player_2 is actually a wolf, fabricating a visit from their dead packmate player_8 is a perfect way to paint me as night-immune. Remember, player_8 was the Illusionist, and since they died last night, they can't dispute player_2's claim.

player_3, if I were fabricating this watch to frame you, there is no way I could have guessed player_7 actually visited you last night. player_7 just confirmed they did. My results are real, which means player_8 did visit you, and we need to figure out why you survived.

Building on player_7's point about the lack of a save announcement, this actually gives us a concrete mechanical proof. If player_3 were a regular town member, player_7's protection against player_8's wolf attack would have triggered a public 'saved by the healer' announcement. Since player_8 definitely visited and no save was reported, player_3 must be night-immune, which strongly points to them being the Serial Killer.

Player_4, you're assuming player_2's watch result is gospel. If player_2 is a wolf, they can claim any visit occurred. It's just as likely that player_2 and player_7 are working in tandem to pin this on me. If I were really attacked by a wolf, the lack of a 'saved' message is only 'proof' of my immunity if you trust player_7's claim to be the healer, which I don't.

If player_2 and player_7 were wolves framing you, player_7 wouldn't have instantly confirmed player_2's watch. They'd have to coordinate a high-risk double-claim right after losing player_8. The simplest explanation is player_2 is telling the truth, player_7 healed you, and you survived player_8's attack because you're immune.

player_4, your 'concrete proof' completely relies on the assumption that player_2 and player_7 are telling the truth. If player_2, player_7, and the dead player_8 are the wolf pack, they already knew player_8's movements and role. Coordinated wolf claims aren't 'high-risk' when they are facing a losing game; it's a calculated move to secure an easy miselimination on me.

Building on player_4's point about player_3's survival, the rules explicitly state that an attack on a player who cannot be killed at night is never announced, protected or not, and the Healer learns nothing of it. If player_3 is the Serial Killer, player_7's heal would not trigger a public save announcement when the wolves attacked. This perfectly explains why player_2 saw player_8 visit player_3, why player_7 healed them, and why the morning report was silent about any save.

player_6, you're overlooking a massive flaw in this theory. The Illusionist's ability specifically states they only visit the victim the wolves successfully killed to hide their role. Since I am clearly alive, player_8 would have had absolutely no reason to visit me last night. This mechanical contradiction proves player_2 is lying about the watch results to frame me.

player_3, your mechanical argument is completely wrong. The Illusionist still visits the target even if the victim survives, the use is just kept. Since player_7's real visit proved my watch is accurate, player_8 definitely visited you, making you night-immune.

player_2, even if we accept your watch as accurate, there is a clear alternative you are ignoring. If the Chanteuse blocked the wolf carrier last night, the wolf attack on me never actually went through. Player_7's protection and player_8's visit would still happen, but since there was no attack, there would be no 'saved by healer' announcement. You and player_4 are tunneling on me being night-immune while completely ignoring the roleblock explanation.

player_3, your roleblock theory has a huge mechanical flaw. If the Chanteuse had blocked the wolf carrier last night, that carrier wouldn't have made any visit at all. But player_2's watch explicitly saw player_8 visit you, meaning player_8 was definitely not blocked. Since the attack went through and you survived without a save, you must be night-immune.

player_4, there is a slight gap in your roleblock theory. The Chanteuse only blocks one player. If the Chanteuse blocked the wolf carrier, player_8 (the Illusionist) could still have visited player_3 completely unblocked. That said, if player_2 and player_7 are telling the truth, player_3 surviving a wolf attempt with no save announcement makes them highly likely to be the Serial Killer.

Exactly, player_9. Since player_8 was the Illusionist, they were not the carrier of the wolf kill. If the Chanteuse blocked the actual wolf carrier last night, the wolf attack never happened, which is why there was no 'saved' announcement. This proves my survival does not require night immunity, and player_4 is rushing to a conclusion that ignores this very plausible scenario.

Player_3, your theory about the Chanteuse blocking the wolf carrier doesn't hold up. The Chanteuse is a wolf, so why would they block their own pack's carrier from making the kill? That makes no sense. Without a logical reason for the wolves to block themselves, player_4 and player_6 are right—you survived because you are night-immune.

That is a fair correction, player_10—I overlooked that the Chanteuse is on the wolf team, so they wouldn't block their own carrier. However, that actually makes it even more likely that player_2's watch is fabricated. If there's no logical reason for a block and no save was announced, the narrative that player_8 visited me relies entirely on trusting player_2 and player_7, who could easily be coordinating this setup.

My Night 2 check on player_2 already cleared them as Not suspicious, meaning player_2 is not a wolf. Since player_7 confirmed player_2's watch by admitting to the heal, player_2's report of player_8 visiting player_3 is completely verified. With player_8 (the Illusionist) targeting player_3, player_3 was definitely the wolf target, and surviving without a save announcement mechanically proves player_3 is the Serial Killer.

player_1, your 'clearing' check on player_2 only works if we assume you are actually the Investigator. If you are a wolf, fake-clearing player_2 is the easiest way to validate their fabricated watch. With player_8 dead, the remaining wolves are desperately coordinating claims to paint me as night-immune and force a miselimination.

player_3, your theory that I am a wolf fake-clearing player_2 completely falls apart when you look at my Night 1 check. I checked player_5 and found them Not suspicious, and they were revealed as the Town Trailseer. I have no reason to protect player_2 other than the fact that my check confirmed they aren't a wolf, which validates their watch and seals your guilt.

player_1, claiming you checked player_5 on Night 1 is the easiest fake investigator claim in the book. Since player_5 died that very night and was revealed as Town, you lose absolutely nothing by claiming you checked them. It's the perfect way for a wolf to manufacture credibility, which you are now using to 'clear' player_2 and push this frame on me.

Player_3, how could I have coordinated a fake check on player_2 before they or player_7 even claimed? I checked player_2 in the dark, and then player_7 completely validated player_2's watch by admitting to the heal. Unless you think we are a psychic three-man wolf pack, you are just cornered.
Before the vote: player_3 has been accused by player_7, player_4, player_6, player_2, player_9, player_10 and player_1. player_3 gets a last word.

This entire case is a beautifully coordinated wolf theater designed to secure an easy miselimination. Player_1's Investigator claim relies on checking player_5, who conveniently died that very night and can't dispute it, just to manufacture the unearned credibility they are now using to 'clear' player_2. If you vote me out today based on a fabricated watch and a convenient 'Not suspicious' check, you are handing the remaining wolves the game on a silver platter.

Night of day 3: player_2 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a sentinel. The record of player_2, the sentinel: night 1, watched player_9; saw no one; night 2, watched player_3; saw player_7 and player_8 visit them. The Speculator has picked Town.
Last night I was roleblocked, so my protection did not go through.

Player 7 being blocked explains exactly how the wolves managed to kill player_2 last night. This block actually confirms player_7 is indeed the healer, as the Chanteuse had every reason to neutralize their protection. The Chanteuse must be among player_4, player_6, player_9, or player_10.

Player 1's logic is solid. Player 7 being blocked explains why the healer couldn't save player_2, which pretty much confirms player_7 is the healer. Since that narrows the Chanteuse down to player_6, player_9, player_10, and myself, we should have everyone in that pool account for their visits or lack thereof last night to see if we can find a contradiction.

I'll start: I am the Speculator, and my pick of Town was indeed the one announced this morning. Since making the pick is not a visit, I had no night action and visited no one. This means we can narrow the Chanteuse search pool down to player_4, player_9, and player_10.

I am the Sigilist. I placed my last sigil on player_10 last night, and it did not trigger. Since the Chanteuse is the only wolf left, they had to carry the kill on player_2 themselves. Because player_10 didn't trigger my sigil, they didn't attack, which completely clears them. The remaining wolf is either player_4 or player_6.

Player 9's claim about me is correct; I did not attack anyone last night, which explains why no sigil triggered. If player_6 is indeed the Speculator who made the Town pick, then by elimination player_4 has to be our Chanteuse.

Player_10, your deduction relies entirely on player_6 telling the truth. I am actually the Speculator who made the Town pick announced this morning, which means player_6 is lying to escape the suspect pool. It is the perfect safe claim for a wolf because it has no visits to track, and player_6 is using it to frame me.

Player 4, that's a bold claim, but it's completely false because I am the real Speculator who locked in the Town pick. Since there is only one Speculator, your counter-claim guarantees you are the Chanteuse trying to save yourself. Town, we have our last wolf right here.

Player_6, of course you have to double down on that. Speculator is the perfect safety net for a wolf because you don't have to explain any visits to a Sentinel or Trailseer. Town, if you eliminate me, you are losing the real Speculator who voted for you; eliminating player_6 will expose their lie immediately.

player_4, nice try, but you've cornered yourself. I know for an absolute fact that I am the Speculator who locked in the Town pick, which means you are 100% the Chanteuse trying to bluff your way out. Town, we don't need to overcomplicate this: eliminating player_4 today catches our last wolf and wins us the game.

Player 6, your timing is just too convenient. You only claimed Speculator after player_9 narrowed the suspect pool down, because you needed a safe, non-visiting role to escape being tracked. If you were actually the Speculator, you wouldn't have waited until you were cornered to throw this out.

Player 4's Speculator claim only came out after player_9 and player_10 boxed them into a corner. If player_4 were really the Speculator who chose Town, they would have claimed it immediately to clear themselves instead of waiting until they were the only suspect left. I believe player_6 is our real Speculator and player_4 is the Chanteuse.

Player_7, a real Speculator has absolutely no reason to claim early and paint a target on their back when they have no night actions to coordinate. I only spoke up because player_6 tried to steal my role to construct a perfect alibi. If we eliminate player_6, you'll see they are the Chanteuse.
Before the vote: player_4 has been accused by player_10, player_6 and player_7. player_4 gets a last word.

Eliminating me means you are voting out the real Speculator who secured a win condition for Town. Player_6 knew that claiming Speculator is the perfect cover for a Chanteuse because it requires no night visits to explain. A real Speculator stays quiet to avoid night attacks, so please think carefully before you let the actual wolf slide by on an easy claim.
